analysis:
Examined the docs-only batch: the new docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md (head 1-103) and configuration.md, where the date changes at line 3 and a new Add-on hold section is added at head 149-164. Base configuration.md text 1-476 is otherwise unchanged context.

The docs describe a new local attack surface: an AF_UNIX `hold.v1` socket at ~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock (0600, in a 0700 directory). Through it, a code-signed add-on (io.darkbloom.sandbox, team SLDQ2GJ6TL, hardened runtime) can make the provider drain or stop serving. Holds use 30-600 s leases, a 120 s drain bound, a 60 s settle bound and ownership.lock flock probing.

Peer verification is described as per-request: the audit token's EUID, then a SecCode guest lookup by audit token (not by PID or path), then a designated requirement. The documented behavior is fail-closed for availability: a lock-probe failure counts as held, and an expiring lease persists while the lock is held. That means a same-user process holding ownership.lock could keep the provider non-serving indefinitely. The doc itself states that same-user files are not a boundary (line 95-97), so this is a DoS by the operator (ADV-001 / TB-003) against their own provider, not consumer exposure.

DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY and the test-only DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET are documented as not in the LaunchAgent passthrough list and not compiled into release builds. None of this can be verified without AddonPeerPolicy.swift, AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonHoldPaths.swift, ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift and LaunchAgent.swift.

Threat-model gap: addon-hold-ipc.md:97 cites threat-model `TB-012`, which is absent from the base canonical index. Integration must confirm that the PR adds TB-012 with threats covering the following:
- peer impersonation;
- forged ownership.lock or addon-hold.json causing a persistent serving hold;
- interaction with the coordinator busy fields (protocol-messages.md#add-on-hold-busy-fields) and with TB-011/T-053 authorization and drain semantics;
- whether a hold suspends inference while proof/challenge handling continues.

The DEBUG-only and release-gating claims also need source verification.

No concrete regression is visible in documentation alone.
